rows.name: U.K. Unique Taxpayer Reference Number
rows.why: The primary element scores 14/40 — a bare run of digits around 10 characters, with no checksum validation. 14 of its 15 supporting keywords are generic, putting keyword quality at 7/100. Every confidence tier requires a keyword within 300 characters, which is what drives the false-negative side.
rows.challenge: Any 10-digit number is a candidate — invoice numbers, order references, unformatted phone numbers and epoch timestamps all collide with it. Its keywords are shared with dozens of other jurisdictions' SITs, so the same document lights up several countries at once. In spreadsheets and CSVs the 300-character window reaches only two or three rows past the header, so most values in a long column never see the keyword.
rows.ckNote: Leading digit is a mod-11 check over the following nine, weights 6,7,8,9,10,5,4,3,2. HMRC publishes the algorithm in its Self Assessment reference checker.
fixes: Use the relaxed-proximity pattern for tabular data
